name: Highlands 39

nadir.desc: The nadir view shows a single-story residence with a complex roofline situated on a large, sparsely vegetated desert parcel|A curved driveway originates from a two-point connection to the public road at the upper portion of the image, loops through the property, and terminates near a detached structure to the right of the main residence|A small patch of irrigated green lawn is visible on the south side of the main structure, and a larger rectangular area of dry grass extends further south|Low-growing desert shrubs and scattered juniper trees are distributed across the surrounding open land, with no fencing visible around the perimeter.

alpha.desc: The alpha view highlights the front of the property as seen from the roadway side|The curved paved driveway is clearly visible approaching the main residence and a detached structure from the public road, with the two driveway access points flanking a landscaped median at the road connection|Multiple juniper trees are scattered along the front approach and around the structures|The main residence has a light-colored stucco exterior with a dark roof, and the detached structure to the right of the main building is also single-story with a similarly styled exterior.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the property from the right side, with the road visible along the right edge of the frame|The detached structure and the rear portion of the main residence are visible, with open desert terrain extending to the left|A cleared, sandy area is present between the structures and the road on this side of the property, and scattered juniper trees are distributed throughout|No fencing, outbuildings, or access gates are visible on this side.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, with the main residence and detached structure visible in the upper portion of the frame|The rear yard consists of open desert terrain with scattered juniper trees and low desert shrubs; no fencing, walls, or rear access gates are visible|The rectangular dry grass area is visible just south of the main structure|The surrounding land to the rear is entirely open and undeveloped, providing unobstructed access to the rear of the structures across relatively flat terrain.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property with the paved road visible along the left edge of the frame|The main residence and a portion of the detached structure are visible, with the tan-colored driveway surface connecting them|Open desert terrain with scattered juniper trees extends to the right of the structures|No fencing, walls, or barriers are present on the left side, leaving the structures directly accessible from the adjacent open land.

considerations: The property is accessed via a curved paved driveway with two connection points to the public road, allowing drive-through access and reducing the need to reverse large vehicles. The surrounding terrain on all sides is open desert with low vegetation, enabling off-road approach to all four sides of the structures across relatively flat ground. Scattered juniper trees are present throughout the property but do not form dense stands that would obstruct vehicle movement near the structures. No perimeter fencing, gates, or walls are visible, meaning the property is open on all sides for responder access and staging.
clarifications: Are both driveway connections to the road open and unobstructed at all times, or is either access point gated or seasonally blocked? What is the surface composition of the driveway — is it paved, packed gravel, or compacted dirt — and can it support the weight of heavy emergency apparatus? Does the detached structure have a separate entry door and what is its use? Are there any propane tanks, fuel storage, or utility shutoffs located on the exterior of the structures that are not visible in the imagery?
